grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.rule: あした｜さんじはんに｜あいます。おしらせを｜よみます。

tables.caption: The tentative hour and the agreed half-hour
Whole polite forms and their chapter objects

grammar.note_en:
The invitation supplies a day, あした, “tomorrow,” but the time field was blank at the end of chapter 3. In this chapter the volunteers distinguish that day from きょう, “today.” A day word alone does not give a clock time. The notice for today is a different notice from the one for tomorrow. The displayed labels refer to the current story day; do not assume an old real-world notice’s printed “today” always means the day on which you happen to read it.

さんじ is the one whole clock-hour expression taught here: three o’clock. The ending じ marks an hour on the clock, but the reading さんじ is taught as a complete expression. Do not derive other hour readings by cutting up ひとつ/ふたつ/みっつ, and do not assume an untaught cardinal-number series. はん adds half an hour after the named hour: さんじはん is three-thirty, not three. The two clock diagrams distinguish the tentative 3:00 proposal from the notice’s 3:30. ごご before a clock time marks p.m. In ordinary day-part reference it can mean afternoon; as a p.m. marker it also applies to later evening hours, so it is not a general rule that ごご excludes よる.

A clock time normally takes に before an action: あした、ごごさんじはんにあいます means “We meet tomorrow at 3:30 p.m.” The people meeting are clear from the conversation; there is no new pronoun hidden in the verb. In めいとれんは、あした、ごごさんじはんにあいます, “Mei and Ren meet tomorrow at 3:30 p.m.,” their names supply the subject. In this chapter きょう and あした are used without に. Do not extend “clock time + に” into a rule that every time word must take に. Compare the already known place relation つくえのうえにあります, “It is on the desk”: the same written particle has different roles in those two constructions.

あさ is morning, ひる is midday or daytime, and よる is night/evening. ひる is not a claim that every mentioned event starts exactly at twelve o’clock. The older notice has programme headings for those parts of today. The relevant new notice instead supplies tomorrow’s particular p.m. clock time. あしたのあさ means “tomorrow morning,” using the familiar の to relate the morning to that day. The rejected morning/night guesses are noun identifications such as あさではありません, not the untaught negative forms of an existence verb.

いつ asks when. In あつまりはいつですか, “When is the gathering?”, the answer can identify the day while the exact clock time is still unsettled. なんじ asks the clock time: あしたなんじにあいますか means “At what time do we meet tomorrow?” This is taught as one whole question expression, not a licence for every later なん compound. Yui also writes いつ as a short when-heading on her own memo; あした below it gives the day, and the separate clock entry gives the time.

The polite nonpast forms よみます, かきます, ききます and あいます mean read, write, ask and meet here. They keep the same form with Yui, Ren or Mei. Nonpast can describe an action taking place now or an arranged future action: あした makes the future reference explicit in あした、さんじはんにあいます. This chapter teaches the shown whole polite forms, not an unrestricted verb paradigm or dictionary forms.

を marks the direct object for reading, writing and asking about a topic. おしらせをよみます means “read the notice”; じかんをかきます means “write the time”; じかんをききます means “ask about the time.” The named field and quoted writing identify where the writing goes. Quoted 「さんじ」をかきます means writing that taught word; the quotation marks do not introduce the later quotative と construction. In めいはききます followed by her spoken key question, the question itself supplies what she asks; no explicit object is needed. In these actual question exchanges, ききます means “ask.” The separate “listen” sense is not taught here.

In じかんのらんにごごさんじはんをかきます, “write 3:30 p.m. in the time field,” に marks the place receiving the writing. That is different from the clock-time に in さんじはんにあいます. Ren initially writes the tentative ごごさんじ on his own invitation. After the correct notice is read, he adds はん beside さんじ, so the written time becomes ごごさんじはん without erasing a different hour.

Yui’s large card is still her name card. She writes the agreed time beneath her name as a personal memo. Mei writes the agreed time on her small invitation; Ren completes the same time by adding はん to his tentative hour. Ren then hands his completed invitation back to Mei, who has the two small invitations in the envelope again. Matching times do not change ownership or turn Yui’s large memo into a third invitation.

かぎ means key. The scene asks about the key for the reading room, whose location has not been established. The volunteers inspect the bag, box and nearby places, but the chapter does not give a hidden successful discovery or teach a negative existential. In C, describe the final search when asked; do not supply a location for the key from imagination. The final question leaves the next practical problem open even though tomorrow’s meeting time has been settled.

notes: Scratch draft only. Parent must apply after chapter3 release, run the actual gate and obtain fresh independent linguistic/pedagogical readiness before finalization.
Original modern Japanese kana narrative; no audio or authentic quotation. Full 30 workbook +8 A +8 B +6 C responses remain in force.

The clock-hour counter retains stable ja-04-03 and lemma じ, with only the explicitly dated whole form さんじ. No いち/に/さん cardinal series or untaught hour is licensed. はん combines with that taught form to show 3:30.
The day on the invitation is read on its front in this chapter; the previous chapter’s reverse-side time field stays blank until the writing scene here.
The key remains unlocated. No negative existence form, imperative, volitional or action-location で is assumed.

Parent inspection replaced the tautological C worked model with retrieval of Yui’s known card size, and the final C key-topic wording with a fully taught question about Ren’s observed search. The parent records bounded G04 clock/interrogative and writing-field licences explicitly; no ceiling or reading/practice target is raised or reduced.

review_questions.question: JA04-Q1 [?] Verify natural contemporary polite Japanese and G04 licensing: day versus clock に, the one bounded hour form, half-hour, read/write/ask/meet valency, and no new case or future verb paradigm.

JA04-Q2 [?] Does the wrong-day notice genuinely explain disagreement and the correct notice establish tomorrow at 3:30 p.m.? Verify all card ownership, handovers and the unchanged blank-field-to-written-field transition.
JA04-Q3 [?] Assess developed narrative/first-use support and all visible cues, models, accepted answers and C stages; do not infer a found key or accept a numerical-volume waiver.
